text.accounts.ts: Checks a pasted token with its provider, stores the account only when the check passes, and renames accounts or sets their expiry or commit email through small named rules
text.accounts.ts gotcha: A failed check stores nothing, and an expiry the provider reports cannot be overridden by hand.
text.bindings.ts: Remembers which profile each project uses per provider, picks the only profile by default and asks for a choice when there are several
text.bindings.ts gotcha: Without a secure store the choices stay in memory and are gone after a restart.
text.credential-server.ts: Listens on the local credential socket and answers each request with the variables an agent run would get for that project and provider, or a typed refusal; a code host account also gets its e-mail as GIT_COMMIT_EMAIL
text.credential-server.ts gotcha: Only the asked provider's variables leave it, one request per connection, size and time capped.
text.credential-server.ts see-also: the in-window channels of the same accounts are answered there, to our own page only
text.credential-server.ts = src/main/auth/ind: takes the injection and the project view from the one composition
text.credential-server.ts = src/main/auth/red: logs requests and refusals with tokens hidden
text.credential-socket.ts: Defines the socket's place per platform, its size and time limits, the request and reply shapes and the request parser
text.credential-socket.ts gotcha: The path follows the profile's user-data folder, so a dev run has its own; Windows uses a per-user pipe.
text.electron-cipher.ts: Adapts the operating system's safeStorage to the cipher the secret store needs, and treats the Linux basic_text backend as unavailable
text.env-names.ts: Lists which credential variable names are set in the environment or in a project's .ai/.env and .env files, names only
text.env-names.ts gotcha: Never returns a value, and skips symlinked or oversized files.
text.errors.ts: Defines the typed errors for provider refresh failures, unavailable tokens and invalid bindings
text.index.ts: Composes the stores, token manager, accounts and project view into one auth service: add a pasted token, bind, unbind, remove an account, and hand an agent run the credentials of a project's accounts
text.ipc.ts: Answers the status, project, add-token, rename, expiry, commit-email, bind, unbind and remove channels for our own workspace page only, validating every argument and never returning a token
text.known-project.ts: Maps a folder to the opened project it belongs to after resolving symlinks, or to nothing when it belongs to none
text.known-project.ts gotcha: A subfolder or worktree of an opened project counts, but a symlink leading out of it does not.
text.outcome.ts: A value-or-error result with a chaining step, so a run of lookups that can each refuse reads as steps instead of early returns
text.private-file.ts: Writes and reads the small JSON files of the sign-in store, owner-readable only
text.profiles.ts: Stores the saved accounts of each provider with login, name, nickname, email, site and expiry, never a secret
text.profiles.ts gotcha: Adding the same account again keeps its profile id, nickname and a saved email, so project choices survive.
text.project-view.ts: Works out a project's code host from its remote and, for GitHub, Bitbucket and Jira alike, the account in use (a chosen one, or by default only for the detected host and Jira), the accounts to choose from, which one is suggested and which credential wins
text.providers.ts: Re-exports the shared provider table, and defines what a provider driver must do to refresh a token and name its account and whether a URL belongs to a provider
text.redact.ts: Hides tokens, codes, verifiers and client secrets in text before it is logged, behind the log prefix of the messages catalogue
text.secret-store.ts: Keeps tokens encrypted on disk, or in memory only when the system cannot encrypt, and says whether one can be read
text.secret-store.ts gotcha: With no encryption available it writes nothing, so a saved token is lost on restart.
text.spawn-env.ts: Turns a project's accounts into the environment variables an agent run gets, never overriding a provider the environment already sets
text.spawn-env.ts gotcha: One explicit variable of a provider, an email say, keeps the whole provider out so credentials never mix.
text.status.ts: Builds the per-provider view of accounts with nickname, email, site and expiry, the account a project uses and its state, with no token fields
text.token-check.ts: Calls GitHub, Bitbucket or Jira with a pasted token to learn the account behind it (GitHub's public e-mail included), retrying Jira through the Atlassian cloud gateway for scoped tokens, with a timeout and a plain text for each failure kind
text.token-check.ts gotcha: A redirect is never followed, so a token cannot be sent to another host.
text.token-manager.ts: Hands out valid access tokens, refreshing once at a time and storing the rotated refresh token first, hands a pasted token back as it is, and tracks whether each account is connected, offline, expired or unavailable
text.token-manager.ts gotcha: A refresh token is deleted only when the provider rejects it, never on a network error.
